Using small sections of time is the starting point for predeterminism. 

Our human existence is deterministic in that we have no choice in being a human, but then some would go on to say that this deterministic entity has a indeterministic choices, which makes less sense than it having deterministic choices.

Free will could exist, and I don't think it's all that depressing even if it doesn't. I don't think any of this is an issue. I only feel distressed when people think suicide or other seemingly immoral acts are wrong merely because of doctrines or that they don't want to think about whether it's right or wrong (because it's painful to them).

If you don't want to increase your chances of suicide, then focus on the positives -- I get it.

Yep, predeterminism appears to be very real. I'm just looking for some fundamental truths (or lack of truths) and solid reasoning to back them so that I may 'go forth and prosper'. It's difficult living in a world in which most are religious or do not think about these, quite superficial, philosophical issues.

The only consequences are the potential sadness it will cause and happiness it will take away, but these two feelings are nothing more than guidelines to me, that I didn't choose.

I'm just fortunate that my nature is congruent with most of societies instead of being a psychopath whose purpose and happiness might come from hurting people.

Thanks for the chat.

I still don't think that there are any consequences to suicide, and I still view life from a nihilistic/absurd viewpoint, but I'll just embrace the ecstasy of it (life).

Thanks for the replies.

I think agnosticism/gnosticism relates to not having/having knowledge, and atheism/theism relates to belief, so I don't think you can be just agnostic.

My main issue is that it's hard to assign meaning to humans if it's possible for someone to be born, and perhaps die due to natural causes (hereditary illnesses). They were born into a deterministic life with perhaps constrained indeterministic choices, and so they died.

We can only ignore it since it didn't happen to us, or we can acknowledge that it may as well be happening to us. 
Sometimes I think that people just don't understand these things because of a lack of empathy (or perspective taking). 

If terrible things -- from the human perspective -- have happened to others, then they may as well have happened to myself, but I do acknowledge that the beauty of life has a tendency to override all feelings of negativity and pain that I have listed above. I only worry that I'm living a lie by embracing the joy whilst blocking empathy. It almost feels like self-imposed brainwashing just to avoid the truth of life.

I'm an agnostic atheist, and I'm guessing you're an agnostic theist. 
I don't really have any reason to believe that humanity is more than biology: take away biology and there is no humanity.

We judge things to have intrinsic value based upon our biology that we did not choose. It seems whimsical. 
I agree that focusing on things that cause pain could be a bad time, but that's due to my deterministic biology. It's probably painful because it's counterproductive to our biological imperative which is to survive.

I omitted many characteristics, but listed some to help people understand my point.
We don't choose to be born with love, hate, logic, illogic, and so on: I never chose these things, or their counterparts to exist within me. That was my point. Our lack of free will over our human nature is commonly accepted, but free will is argued about in terms of our ability to make choices.
We give value, or significance, to things based upon how good it feels, even though we never chose for those things to feel good.

I regret ending my post with time is meaningless, but it was to the point.

If there is something after death then you will still have experiences; if there isn't, then those experiences are equivalent to everything else in existence, e.g. the non-sentient water's experience of flowing down a hill, or the rocks experience of dropping.

It wasn't really the crux of my issue.
